lb-vm3n.title: Add Trapper Keeper wiki sync discipline to trk prime
lb-vm3n.description:
Goal: add standing `trk prime` guidance so agents treat Trapper Keeper as shared project memory and keep it synchronized proactively, not only when asked.

Problem observed:
- An agent updated `.trapper_keeper` locally, committed local wiki notes, then discovered the remote `trapperkeeper` branch had newer history.
- The push became non-fast-forward and required a conflict-heavy merge.
- Root cause: the agent treated the wiki as local notes first and sync target second.

Repository layout clarification:
- Normal case: Trapper Keeper state belongs to the same repo being worked on, usually on that repo's orphan `trapperkeeper` branch.
- Alternate supported case: Trapper Keeper can be initialized in-tree, so wiki files are normal repo files at the configured path.
- Less common case: a coordination repo may contain wiki/planning state for multiple separate service repos. Do not make this the default mental model in `trk prime`; phrase guidance around "the repo's Trapper Keeper wiki" and only mention separate coordination repos as an edge case.

Desired model:
- If a repo has Trapper Keeper initialized, treat its wiki as shared project memory, not local scratch.
- `trk` should prime agents to use a remote-first, continuously synchronized workflow for both orphan-branch and in-tree modes.
- This applies broadly to any repo using Trapper Keeper, not just one project.

Proposed `trk prime` language:

## Trapper Keeper Wiki Discipline

If this repo has Trapper Keeper initialized, treat its wiki as shared project memory, not local scratch. The usual layout is an orphan `trapperkeeper` branch exposed at `.trapper_keeper/`; some repos may use an in-tree wiki directory instead. Rare coordination repos may host wiki/planning state for multiple service repos, but that is not the default case.

Before reading or editing the wiki:
- Fetch the wiki remote.
- In orphan-branch mode, integrate the remote `trapperkeeper` branch before making new edits.
- In in-tree mode, integrate the repo's normal remote branch before making wiki edits.
- Never overwrite remote wiki history with force push unless explicitly instructed.

During meaningful work, keep the wiki current:
- Add or update pages for decisions, PRs, branches, investigations, blockers, and shipped behavior.
- Update `log.md` with dated work entries.
- Update `toc.md` for navigable pages.
- Update `index.md` with searchable concepts, branches, tickets, PRs, and important file/module names.
- Preserve raw sources under `sources/` when external/raw material is used.

At the end of wiki-relevant work:
- Run a conflict-marker / whitespace check.
- Commit wiki changes separately from service-code changes when the wiki is in orphan-branch mode.
- In in-tree mode, keep wiki changes logically separate from code changes where practical.
- Pull/fetch again if needed, merge remote wiki changes, resolve conflicts by preserving useful content from both sides.
- Push the wiki updates: `trapperkeeper` for orphan-branch mode, or the normal repo branch for in-tree mode.
- Report the commit hash and whether the wiki is clean.

Do not wait for the user to ask for routine wiki updates. Do this proactively whenever work creates durable context another session or machine will need.

Additional guardrails:
- Do not mix service repo changes with orphan-branch wiki commits.
- Do not leave Trapper Keeper wiki changes dirty at end of turn unless the user explicitly asks to pause before committing/pushing.

Possible tooling follow-up:
- Consider adding `trk sync` / `trk publish` helpers so agents do not have to remember the exact git sequence.
- The prime rule still matters even with tooling: fetch first, write continuously, index, commit, merge, push.
- Tooling should account for both orphan-branch mode and in-tree mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- `trk prime` output includes the discipline above, or an equivalent concise version that preserves every operational requirement.
- The output clearly frames orphan-branch mode as the normal/default case and in-tree mode as supported.
- The output does not imply the Augmenta-style "outer coordination repo plus separate service repos" layout is typical.
- Tests covering `prime` output are updated to assert the new sync/proactive-update expectations.
- Any docs that describe `prime`, wiki storage modes, or wiki update triggers are updated to match.
